conventions.convention: Germ multiplication is ordinary composition. The fundamental-group product traverses the first loop first, so homomorphic holonomy uses transport along the reversed loop.

C¹ leaves carry their intrinsic plaque topology; compactness means compactness in that topology. C¹ coorientation means increasing transverse transitions. Smooth coorientation is separately defined by a nowhere-zero smooth defining form.
ACω is choice for a sequence of nonempty sets. Full AC is an explicit additional hypothesis of the finite-CW, cohomological-stability and global-stability chains.

A stable leaf has arbitrarily small saturated open neighborhoods. Smooth foliated gluing requires matching plane-field jets in signed collar coordinates; matching boundary foliations alone is insufficient.

For the mapping-torus action n·(x,t)=(fⁿ(x),t+n), positive-time return on the fibre is f⁻¹. Global stability concerns a closed boundaryless ambient manifold; the boundary/interval variant is excluded.
Modules are unital left modules over arbitrary unital rings. A kernel for A-Mod→B-Mod is a (B,A)-bimodule; its right action on F(A) is ma=F(r_a)(m).
Functor-category and biequivalence language for all modules is schematic for fixed definable functor schemas; natural transformations have set codes. Proper-class functors are not set-coded objects.
A Morita 1-cell A→B is a (B,A)-bimodule M; composition with N:B→C is N⊗_B M. Reconstruction uses A=End(P)ᵒᵖ and action eᵒᵖ·h=h∘e.
Small means that Hom(P,-) preserves every set-indexed coproduct. General category reconstruction additionally requires supplied definable copower and cokernel assignments.

load_bearing.statement: For unital rings A,B and an additive, right exact, coproduct-preserving F:A-Mod→B-Mod, the canonical comparison F(A)⊗_A-→F is a natural isomorphism. No commutativity or choice is used.
For (B,A)-bimodules M,M′, evaluation at A gives inverse bijections Nat(T_M,T_M′)≅Hom_{B-A}(M,M′), with every component η_X=f⊗1_X; these respect addition, identities and vertical composition.

Assuming ACω, a compact leaf of a smooth regular foliation with finite holonomy is stable and has arbitrarily small saturated finite-holonomy normal-model neighborhoods. Their leaves are compact with finite holonomy and finitely covered by the holonomy cover; a retraction onto the original leaf restricts to finite coverings on leaves and has transverse-disk fibres.

Under ACω, a compact smooth finite-holonomy leaf, fixed tubular fibres and a sufficiently small invariant disk admit a smooth transport map Φ:Ĺ×D→M with Φ(hŷ,ht)=Φ(ŷ,t), central restriction p, and each slice mapping into the leaf through t. Actual representatives are a compatible finite family.

Assuming full AC, for a smooth cooriented codimension-one foliation of a closed connected smooth manifold with a compact finite-fundamental-group leaf L, the union of compact leaves diffeomorphic to L is closed, hence all of M; all leaves have trivial holonomy.
A compact leaf with trivial C¹ holonomy in a transversely oriented C¹ codimension-one foliation has a saturated open neighborhood C¹-foliated-diffeomorphic to L×D with the slice foliation.
Every nontrivial finitely generated subgroup of orientation-preserving C¹ local-diffeomorphism germs fixing 0 admits a surjective homomorphism to Z.

A locally small cocomplete abelian category with a small projective generator P and supplied definable copower and cokernel assignments is equivalent, through Hom(P,-), to left modules over End(P)ᵒᵖ; the constructed adjunction has invertible unit and counit.
For a (B,A)-bimodule M, M⊗_A- is left adjoint to Hom_B(M,-), whose left A-action is (aφ)(m)=φ(ma), with the displayed currying bijection, unit, counit and triangle identities.
The specified Morita tensor composition, canonical associators and unitors satisfy functoriality, pentagon and triangle identities over arbitrary unital rings, without choice.

concerns.concern: F4, line 58, asserts: 'smooth maps out of the pieces of a manifold glued along a boundary, agreeing on overlaps, glue to a smooth map'. Boundary agreement alone does not imply smoothness: the functions -s on s≤0 and s on s≥0 agree at the seam but glue to |s|. Neither cited definition supplies the asserted rule. The proposition's actual proof gives explicit compatible collars and separately checks foliation jets, so this finding concerns the false unrestricted Fact, not a counterexample to the S³ construction.

Step 1.1 says to choose disjoint neighborhoods of z and 'each y∈K', then asserts that no full-AC theorem is invoked. As written this resembles an arbitrary-index selection, although the choice-free proof closes immediately by taking all eligible neighborhood pairs, extracting a finite cover, and selecting only its finitely many partners. The compact-to-Hausdorff claim remains valid.
